Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The study's primary purpose was to determine the impact of the Audio Haptic Maze (AHM) videogame on the development of Orientation and Mobility (O&M) skills in blind learners, clearly indicating a utility-first objective. While the design incorporated videogame elements like mazes, jewelry boxes, keys, and treasures (chunk_3), and users found the experience enriching and associated it with a typical videogame (chunk_5), the core evaluation focused on cognitive impact on O&M skills, with the instrument designed and validated by special education teachers who are specialists in visual disabilities (chunk_8). This suggests that the utilitarian mechanic of O&M skill development was the primary design driver, with fun elements integrated to enhance engagement rather than being the sole or equally weighted initial focus.

        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The study describes the Audio Haptic Maze (AHM) videogame as designed to develop 'Orientation and Mobility (O&M) skills' in blind learners. Players navigate mazes, find objects, and make 'intelligent decisions' about direction using haptic and audio feedback. This indicates the game relies entirely on the player's skill in navigation and spatial reasoning, with no mention of chance elements.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely solo (i.e., solitaire),
        (2) mostly solo (i.e., playing against AI in single-player StarCraft),
        (3) mix of solo and social affordances (i.e., animal crossing),
        (4) mostly social, but aspects are independent (i.e., house on hill haunt transition),
        (5) entirely social (i.e., tag)
reasoning: The context states that the video game Audio Haptic Maze (AHM) was designed to be used by learners "either autonomously or with the supervision of a facilitator" (chunk_2). The description of the game involves a single player navigating mazes from a first-person perspective, finding items, and interacting via a keyboard and haptic device (chunk_3). This indicates an individual, single-player experience, aligning with an "entirely solo" design, where a facilitator's role is supervisory rather than interactive within the game itself.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: The game 'Audio Haptic Maze (AHM)' is described as allowing a learner to 'navigate through a series of mazes from a first-person perspective' with 'interaction... carried out through the use of a standard computer keyboard'. This implies continuous, real-time control and interaction, where actions can be taken at any time, which aligns best with an 'entirely simultaneous' design rather than turn-based or phased gameplay.

        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: The Audio Haptic Maze (AHM) videogame is described as allowing a single learner to navigate mazes from a first-person perspective, interacting in real-time using a standard computer keyboard and/or a haptic device to receive immediate audio and haptic feedback. This continuous, direct interaction without any mention of delayed or turn-based elements indicates an entirely synchronous design.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely competitive (i.e., spit card game),
        (2) mostly competitive, but sometimes collaboration is important (i.e., forbidden island),
        (3) mix of competitive and collaborative (i.e., mario party 2 vs 2 mini-games),
        (4) mostly collaborative (i.e., animal crossing),
        (5) entirely collaborative (i.e., pandemic)
reasoning: The Audio Haptic Maze (AHM) game is described as a single-player experience where a 'learner' navigates mazes from a 'first-person perspective' to find items and develop O&M skills. There is no mention of other players, competition, or collaborative tasks between players. The game is designed for individual skill development, making it entirely non-competitive. Interpreting 'collaborative' as the player working with the game system towards a shared goal (skill development and maze completion), option (5) 'entirely collaborative' is the best fit as it signifies a complete absence of competitive elements.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: The Audio Haptic Maze (AHM) videogame has a consistent core objective of navigating mazes and finding items, which is symmetrical. However, it offers three distinct interfaces (haptic, audio, and haptic plus audio) that provide different feedback mechanisms and interaction methods, introducing asymmetrical elements to the player's experience.
